skill.name: openserv-agent-sdk
skill.description: Guide developers through creating, provisioning, running, deploying, and troubleshooting OpenServ agents with TypeScript and the OpenServ SDK.
skill.summary: Build and deploy TypeScript agents for the OpenServ platform.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from TypeScript template literals, Markdown fences, documented URLs, or placeholder environment variables. The confirmed risks are legitimate but sensitive OpenServ patterns: wallet private keys, API keys, auth tokens, and payment or on-chain operations require careful handling.

remediation.issue: Wallet private keys and OpenServ credentials are stored or loaded through environment files.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to keep .env and .openserv.json out of version control, restrict file permissions, and rotate keys after accidental exposure.

remediation.issue: Payment, USDC top-up, and ERC-8004 registration workflows can spend funds or gas.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval for paid workflows, credit top-ups, and on-chain registration before running generated commands.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance includes a force-kill command for port conflicts.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a safer command that shows the process first, then asks users to confirm before terminating it.

content.value_statement: Developers need clear guidance to build OpenServ agents without missing platform requirements. This skill explains SDK patterns, provisioning, deployment, troubleshooting, and agent workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to define OpenServ agents with system prompts and capabilities.
Shows runless and runnable capability patterns with Zod schemas.
Documents platform-delegated generation through the SDK generate method.
Guides provisioning, triggers, local runtime, tunnel behavior, and deployment.
Covers task, workspace file, payment, and ERC-8004 identity workflows.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for credentials, ports, tunnels, and module imports.
limitations: It is documentation, not a live OpenServ account or hosted runtime.
It may lag behind current OpenServ SDK releases unless the skill is updated.
Some workflows require OpenServ credentials, wallet funding, or platform access.
Users remain responsible for securing API keys, auth tokens, and wallet private keys.

use_cases.title: Create a First Agent
use_cases.description: Follow the basic agent pattern to provision and run a TypeScript OpenServ agent.

use_cases.title: Deploy Platform Workflows
use_cases.description: Prepare agents for webhook, manual, cron, or x402 triggers with correct runtime settings.

use_cases.title: Add On-Chain Identity
use_cases.description: Use the ERC-8004 guidance to register an agent identity after provisioning.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a simple OpenServ agent. Include the agent purpose, one capability, required packages, and provisioning steps.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Tool to a Capability
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this tool idea into an OpenServ runnable capability. Include input fields, validation needs, task logging, and expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Provisioning Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this OpenServ agent startup error. Explain likely causes, credential checks, and the safest next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production OpenServ workflow with deployment, trigger choice, credential handling, timeout settings, and ERC-8004 considerations.

output_examples.input: I want a webhook agent that summarizes customer notes.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with the agent purpose, capability list, trigger choice, provisioning sequence, timeout guidance, and deployment notes.

output_examples.input: My ERC-8004 registration fails after provisioning.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering wallet funding, private key loading, retry behavior, and how to keep the agent running.

output_examples.input: Should this capability be runless or runnable?
output_examples.output: A recommendation that compares platform-handled generation against custom code, then explains schema and logging requirements.

best_practices: Use runless capabilities or generate when platform-delegated model calls are enough.
Keep user API keys, auth tokens, and wallet private keys out of logs and commits.
Call provision before deployment and confirm trigger timeouts match expected workloads.
anti_patterns: Do not use the legacy process method unless direct OpenAI calls are required.
Do not reuse agent API keys for PlatformClient management calls.
Do not clear wallet state unless you intentionally want a new on-chain identity.

faq.question: Does this skill create an OpenServ account?
faq.answer: No. It explains how provision can create or bind account credentials during agent setup.

faq.question: Do I need an OpenAI API key?
faq.answer: Usually no. Runless capabilities and generate use platform-delegated model calls.

faq.question: Can it help with deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers local runtime, OpenServ Cloud deployment, and self-hosted endpoint configuration.

faq.question: Does it support paid workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents x402 triggers and payment workflows that require careful user approval.

faq.question: What secrets need protection?
faq.answer: Protect OPENSERV_USER_API_KEY, OPENSERV_API_KEY, OPENSERV_AUTH_TOKEN, and WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY.

faq.question: Should I read openserv-client too?
faq.answer: Yes. The companion client reference covers platform management and deeper ERC-8004 APIs.
